title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
grouping: Two stacked sub-diagrams, each titled in underlined italic ('Action Chunking', 'Action Chunking + Temporal Ensemble'). Both are grids: timestep numbers 0-7 run along the top as column heads and query times (t=0, t=4 with a vertical ellipsis between; then t=0..t=3) label the rows on the left. No containers beyond the grid itself.
shapes_depth: Each predicted action is a small flat square with a thin dark outline, filled red, orange, yellow or green by its position within a chunk of four. In the upper grid chunks tile end to end; in the lower grid each row shifts one column right, forming a staircase. Light-grey rounded outlines enclose each column of overlapping predictions; the column at timestep 3 has a black outline, and beside it the inline text 'x [0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.1] =' leads to one yellow square with a soft glow (the combined action).
proposed_highlight: The one column being combined is ringed in black (others in grey) and its weighted sum is written inline next to it; the result square glows.
lesson: Lay predicted actions on a time x query-step grid of coloured squares (colour = position within the chunk) so overlapping chunks form a staircase, and ring one column to show which predictions are averaged for that timestep.
notes: Method short name ACT (Action Chunking with Transformers) from the paper's caption of Figure 4. Venue RSS from Semantic Scholar (title match, venue_source: semantic-scholar); year 2023 = S2 year and arXiv year. flow 'mixed': time runs left to right, query steps top to bottom.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
